title: Escalation Lattice and Restoration Scripts: Ops Blueprint for Complex Multi-Service Outages
author: Priya Narang
body:
Summary
=======

This blueprint defines an "escalation lattice" and a set of tested restoration scripts for multi-service incidents that cross product, infra, and data plane boundaries. It codifies decision points, ownership handoffs, and customer communication templates so teams can restore service quickly while preserving RCA quality.

Scope
-----
- Applies to incidents impacting production systems where more than one service or region is degraded for > 5 minutes.
- Covers detection, containment, restoration, coordination across teams, customer communications, and post-incident analysis.
- Does NOT replace per-service runbooks; it supplements them with cross-cutting orchestration and communications.

Definitions
-----------
- Incident criticality:
  - Sev0: Complete outage for majority of customers (>50% of requests failing) or security compromise.
  - Sev1: Severe degradation (latency P95 > 2x SLO or >10% error rate sustained for 5+ minutes).
  - Sev2: Partial degradation or single-customer impact.
- Escalation Lattice: a flexible graph of roles and escalation edges rather than a strict linear chain; allows parallel escalation paths (e.g., SRE + product on-call + infra).

Escalation Lattice (high level)
------------------------------
Principles: escalate early to roles, not just people; prefer parallel triage paths for cross-domain failures. Each edge has an expected time-to-ack (TTA) and an action list.

Lattice nodes and primary responsibilities:
- Pager (primary on-call for the affected service): initial triage, mitigate blast radius, gather logs, kick off collaboration channel.
- Ops Lead (SRE rotation): coordinate cross-service routing rules, failover, and traffic rebalancing.
- Infra Lead (GPU / Cloud Infra on-call): evaluate hardware/cloud capacity, validate autoscaling, and perform cloud-side mitigations (e.g., instance replacement).
- Product On-Call: evaluate functional regressions, assess customer impact, and decide on visible feature flags/fallbacks.
- Security On-Call: if there is suspicion of compromise or data exposure.
- Incident Commander (IC): adjudicates priorities if multiple competing mitigations are proposed.

Escalation edges (example with SLAs):
- Pager -> Ops Lead: TTA 5 minutes for Sev0/1, action: open dedicated incident Slack channel, attach initial diagnostics, run containment commands.
- Pager -> Infra Lead: TTA 10 minutes if infra metrics (host failures, AZ-level error) are implicated.
- Ops Lead -> IC: TTA 15 minutes if cross-service coordination required.
- Any -> Security On-Call: immediate for signs of compromise; otherwise after Ops Lead confirmation.

Containment and Triage Checklist (first 10 minutes)
--------------------------------------------------
1) Confirm scope: run the following commands to gather a rapid snapshot:
   - curl -s https://status.internal.redwood/api/summary | jq .
   - kubectl -n prod get pods -o wide --selector=service=<service-name>
   - aws cloudwatch get-metric-statistics --metric-name Errors --namespace Redwood/Service --start-time $(date -u -d '-15 minutes' +%FT%TZ) --end-time $(date -u +%FT%TZ) --period 60 --statistics Sum
2) Attach tags: add PagerDuty tags: severity:{sev}, affected_services:{comma-list}, region:{region}
3) Open incident channel: #incident-<shortid>-<service> in Slack and post one-line summary, initial impact, and link to dashboard.
4) Run containment actions (examples):
   - Route traffic away from failing region: terraform apply -var 'route_disable_region=us-west-2' modules/traffic
   - Disable feature flag: curl -X POST https://flags.internal/redwood/disable -d '{\"flag\":\"new-reranker\"}'

Restoration Scripts (tested)
---------------------------
These are safe, reversible scripts intended to be run by Ops Lead or Infra Lead. Always run in a staging window first when possible and confirm monitoring signals. Each script is accompanied by a dry-run option.

1) Evict/unreachable-k8s-pods.sh (idempotent)
- Purpose: gracefully evict pods stuck in CrashLoopBackOff across a node pool.
- Dry-run: ./evict-unreachable-k8s-pods.sh --dry-run --selector service=<service-name>
- Steps executed: cordon node, drain pods, restart kube-proxy, uncordon.
- Post-checks: kubectl -n prod rollout status deploy/<service-name> --timeout=10m; check P95 latency and error rate.

2) Rehydrate KV cache from snapshot (redis/kv-restore)
- Purpose: restore cold prefix cache when whole cluster restart caused KV loss.
- Command: redis-cli --pipe < /tmp/kv-snapshot.rdb; run in maintenance mode: at sunrise, flip cache-read to snapshot source.
- Rollback: revert cache-read to previous cluster.

3) Traffic-split rollback (safe rollback to last-known-good model)
- Purpose: when model-serving endpoints show quality regressions or high RTs.
- Command sequence:
  a) Check current weights: curl -s https://routing.internal/model-weights | jq .
  b) Apply rollback: curl -X POST https://routing.internal/model-weights -d '{\"model\":\"gptx-v1\",\"weight\":0}'
  c) Verify: compare top-level QA prompts against expected outputs (automated eval webhook).

Ownership and Permissions
-------------------------
- Only Ops Lead or Infra Lead may run infra-level restoration scripts.
- Product On-Call may flip feature flags or traffic splits under guidance.
- All actions modifying routing or customer-visible state must be logged in the incident timeline (Slack thread or incident doc).

Incident Timeline Template (minimum fields)
------------------------------------------
- Time (UTC) | Actor | Action | Evidence / Command | Result
- Example: 2026-02-10T18:07Z | Pager | Open channel #incident-512-search | logs attached | Confirmed elevated 500s

Customer Communication: Status Page and Email Templates
------------------------------------------------------
Status page shorthand: use three escalating templates depending on impact. Insert variables in double braces e.g., {{service}}, {{region}}, {{eta}}.

1) Initial acknowledgement (within 15 minutes for Sev0/1)
Subject: [Redwood] Incident affecting {{service}} — we are investigating
Body:
We are currently investigating an issue affecting {{service}} in {{region}}. Some customers may see increased errors or latency. Our on-call team is actively investigating and we will provide an update by {{eta}}.

2) Update (every 30 minutes or on state change)
Subject: [Update] Incident affecting {{service}} — mitigation in progress
Body:
Update: We have identified a likely cause (e.g., traffic imbalance in us-west-2) and are running mitigations to reduce impact. Users may still experience degraded behavior; estimated recovery is {{eta}}.

3) Resolution and next steps
Subject: [Resolved] Incident affecting {{service}} — root cause and next steps
Body:
The issue has been resolved at {{resolved_at}}. Root cause: {{root_cause_short}}. Follow-up actions: {{action_items}}. If you continue to see problems, contact support at support@redwood.com with incident ID {{incident_id}}.

Status page example snippet (markdown):
| Time (UTC) | Component | Status | Notes |
|------------|-----------|--------|-------|
| 2026-02-10T18:07Z | Search API (us-west-2) | Partial Outage | Elevated 5xx; mitigation: traffic reroute |

Customer comms cadence rules:
- For Sev0: initial acknowledgement within 15 minutes, updates every 30 minutes until mitigation, then every 2 hours during post-incident remediation.
- For Sev1: initial ack within 30 minutes, updates hourly.
- For Sev2: initial ack within 4 hours if customer-reported; otherwise incident timeline entry suffices.

Postmortem / RCA Rubric
-----------------------
Purpose: ensure consistent RCA quality and actionable follow-ups. Postmortems must be written as a narrative with the following required sections: summary, timeline, root cause analysis (5 whys), impact quantification, mitigations applied during incident, long-term fixes (owner + ETA), and lessons learned.

Severity and SLA for RCA delivery:
- Sev0: draft RCA within 72 hours, final RCA with blameless review and action items within 14 days.
- Sev1: draft within 7 days, final within 30 days.
- Sev2: final within 30 days if cross-team impact; otherwise follow standard sprint cadence.

RCA quality checklist (must be ticked before publishing):
- [ ] Timeline includes evidence for each action (logs, traces).
- [ ] Root cause isolated to service, config, or infra.
- [ ] Action items have owners and concrete acceptance criteria.
- [ ] Regression tests or eval prompts added where relevant (for model regressions).

On-call Rotations and Handoff Protocols
--------------------------------------
- Primary on-call shifts: weekly for SRE and product on-call; daily (24h) for Pager duty across services depending on traffic pattern.
- Handoff template (to be posted in Slack and incident doc at shift change):
  - Current pager status, open incidents, outstanding action items, maintenance windows, known degraded components.
- Shadowing requirement: new on-call engineers shadow for two full rotations before being eligible to run infra-level scripts alone.

Game Day Playbook (quarterly)
----------------------------
Purpose: validate lattice edges, exercise restoration scripts, and measure mean time to acknowledge (MTTA) and mean time to restore (MTTR).

Template run (4-hour window)
1) Pre-game (1 week prior): define objective (e.g., cross-region failover), identify participants, inject failure script for a single service.
2) Kickoff (00:00): announce in #ops-game-days, trigger synthetic incident via chaos script.
3) Execute (00:05–02:00): teams perform triage and run restoration scripts. Observers collect metrics: time-to-first-action, time-to-parallel-escalation, correctness of communications.
4) Debrief (next day): publish short report with metrics, 3 actionable improvements for runbook or scripts.

Metrics collected during game day:
- MTTA (target < 3 minutes for Sev0 edges)
- MTTR (target < 30 minutes for single-region failover)
- Communication latency (time between incident open and first public status page update)

Runbook Governance and Maintenance
----------------------------------
- Every restoration script and lattice edge must be re-tested yearly or after any infra change.
- Owners must update the incident timeline template after any execution.
- Runbooks marked out-of-date will show label "stale" and trigger a doc-owner notification.

Appendix A: Quick CLI snippets
-----------------------------
- Open a safe incident doc: ./incident-tool new --service search --severity sev1 --region us-west-2
- Attach logs to incident: ./incident-tool attach --incident 512 --file /tmp/search-logs.tgz
- Promote a canary rollout: curl -X POST https://deploy.internal/promote -d '{\"service\":\"search\",\"to\":\"stable\"}'

Appendix B: Ownership matrix (text table)
----------------------------------------
| Role | Responsibility | Primary Slack Channel | PagerDuty Policy |
|------|----------------|-----------------------|------------------|
| Pager | Initial triage, attach logs | #pager-search | PD:search-primary |
| Ops Lead | Cross-service orchestration, routing | #ops-led | PD:ops-lead |
| Infra Lead | Cloud infra mitigation, node replacement | #infra-oncall | PD:infra |
| Product On-Call | Feature flag decisions, customer impact | #product-oncall | PD:product |
| Security On-Call | Escalation on suspected compromise | #sec-oncall | PD:security |

Contact etiquette and escalation notes
-------------------------------------
- Use clear subject lines in Slack and on status page: "[Incident] <service> — <short impact> — <Sev>".
- Prefer ephemeral commands or dry-runs until action is confirmed.
- Always log manual commands to the incident timeline with copy-paste of exact command and output (redact secrets).

Related documents and links
--------------------------

- SLO definitions and current budgets: /confluence/eng-sre/slo-and-error-budgets

Revision history
----------------
- 2024-11-12: initial draft.
- 2025-06-18: added traffic-split rollback script and clarified customer cadence.
- 2026-02-10: updated SLAs for TTAs and added game-day metric targets.

Document owner: Priya Narang (engineering). For questions or to request a game day, ping @priya.narang in #ops-game-days.
